findings.title: Recovery accepts the same artifacts through a replaced plan-root pathname
findings.evidence: recover_fresh_plan_creation_anchor immediately resolves root, then authenticates only the commitment, receipt, and plan bytes and their embedded identifiers. Neither commitment nor receipt records an expected root path or root identity. Independent probe: publish the valid synthetic plan/commitment/receipt, rename the original root, replace its old pathname with a symlink to the moved original root, then call the recovery API with the original pathname. It succeeds with creation-anchor-recovered. Thus root-path replacement is not a fail-closed condition, despite the requested gate.
findings.impact: The recovery path cannot distinguish the originally published plan root from a subsequently replaced or aliased root path. Required replaced-root rejection remains unproven and is directly contradicted for the symlink replacement case.
findings.recommendation: Bind the intended root identity/path into the caller-pinned commitment and durable receipt, or define and implement an equivalent race-safe root identity contract; reject symlinked/replaced roots before recovery. Add subprocess/real-filesystem replacement tests for symlink and directory replacement. Preserve content verification and full verify-fresh-plan requirement.
